[WP] You wake up in prison. In your cell and others surrounding, are fantasy creatures. Some beautiful, some terrifying.

I'm falling. I can't hold on. I'm slipping. Oh God help me I-

... It was a dream. I'm lying on a cold hard floor, and from how heavy my body feels I am definitely not falling. I flex my hand on the ground just in front of my face and close my eyes again. Moving right now seems a silly idea. I'm just going to lie here and let the world pass me by.

Wait.

Where is here?

I open my eyes again then wince at the bright light as I try to look up. You'd never think I use these eyes for seeing outside, judging by the pain that shoot through them, but eventually I force them into action. Only to doubt the first thing they see. A centaur. Just sat there, behind the bars across from me. Bored, like he tried to do a crossword puzzle for 3 hours only to discover that his flight was still delayed.

Would a Centaur even catch a plane? Yes Vincent, that is the question to ask. Would a Centaur catch a plane? Not, are you on drugs, or are you still dreaming, or why can't you remember how you got here? No we have to question the viability of a four legged man and his ability to travel via aviation.

"Oh look. The human lookalike is awake." The sentence was said like the idea of anything looking human was disgusting.

That means it's probably a goblin. I got up and turned around with the minimum effort required to- Aww fuck it is a goblin, look at the ugly bastard, how does his mother even love that face? Of course the ugly runt wasn't the only intriguing thing. He was also sat next to a Satyr that look ready to kick the living shit out of, well, the living shit. And behind him in other cells were Minotaurs, a Cyclops, an underage Troll, few Faun and of course, a Gargoyle doing pullups as he tried to impress the only female inhabitant of the cells - a Succubus. Who I could barely see as men (Or things close to that) were clamouring around the bars of her cell trying to talk to her in the vain hope that their words would seduce her. Not the way it works guys.

"So what is you then? Cause you look awfy like a human to me but but, you don't seem scared of nothing in 'ere. Not even that fuck ugly troll."

"Speak for yourself mate."

The Satyr turned to pay attention now, probably hoping to get some mild entertainment from what came next. The Goblin - like any old Goblin would - took offence. "Oh. I see the way it is. Little special creamfacer thinks that because he can pretend to be human he is somehow better looking than us all."

"Just you mate. Just you."

He got up and made his way towards me, face contorted in disgust. At least, I think it's contorted because of that. "Now look here you runt I'll-"

I decided I couldn't be bothered with him anymore. I opened my mouth and out came the echoing brilliance that was my voice. The heavenly, angelic outpouring of sound that you wrote highschool love songs about. "You'll what my friend..."

Oh how the tables turn. It doesn't work as well on magical beings as it does humans, but he knows what I am immediately. I can almost hear the creatures around me sit up in fright. The goblin himself falls on his arse in sheer surprise.

"Uh, umm, look runt. I, eh, I didn't mean any harm, a'ight?"

I stood up and cracked my back. Stretching out, I simply grinned back at him as the poor Goblin looked up at my slender frame with terror. The disgusting piece of shit will probably have dreams imagining he was as handsome as me for months. Marble sculptors could try for decades and not chisel out a masterpiece as well refined and stunning as this body, not as strong and firm, not as delicate but powerful. And personally, I like to think I'm rather humble about the whole thing.

"Oh really friend? Well that's fine then. I wouldn't want anybody to..." I smiled as the joke crossed my mind. "Hurt themselves."

Now even the Satyr looked uncomfortable. I turned my head to look around the cells and found myself the attention of everybody in the cell complex. Oh the benefits of being one of me. The constant attention and love thrown in my, well, ok, love maybe isn't the correct word. Maybe an incredibly misplaced lust would be more accurate, but you know the thought is there and that's all that matters right? I winked at the Succubus who giggled and faked a bite in my direction, my danger being a thrill to her. I don't know how humans manage to even resist those things for more than a few seconds, I want to fuck their brains out the moment they look in my direction, but then again, maybe that says a lot about my taste in women...

I walked across to my cell and sat next to the Satyr, who shuffled up and gave me more room. "Oh calm yourself boy I'm not planning on trying to get any of you to hang yourself or anything. I've got a blistering headache and I can't tell if it's because of whatever the fuck captured me... or the fact that I was probably out getting totally pissed the same night."

The Satyr attempted a weak smile. "Eh eh eh if it's-"

Oh for fucks sake. "Speak to me like you normally would friend. Please..."

The Satyr sat up perfectly straight, instantly more comfortable and said, "If it's any consolation when I arrived here my head hurt for days. I think they have someone who can find magical beings and hunt them down by entering your brain or something."

I went to speak before the Satyr added. "And could you please not do that again. If you hadn't told me to speak normally I would be crying in fear right now."

I sighed heavily. "I promise not to speak in that way that freaks you the fuck out." I glared at him. "Happy?"

"Better." He mumbled.

"Good." I pointed past the bars to the corridor and double doors, the obvious exit for this hellhole, made more obvious by the obtuse emergency exit sign above the door. "Please, for the love of all things mythical, tell me we haven't been captured by fucking humans. Because I don't know any other being on the planet that would feel the need to put a big green glowing sign saying 'oh hey look this is the only door that doesn't lead into a cell maybe you should try to run the fuck away from a fire in THIS direction', above, the only door, that doesn't lead into a cell."

My lil' Satyr friend didn't appreciate my lame attempt at humour. "Sorry. They are human."

I mean seriously, does he think I come out with speels like that because it makes me feel better about myself as a person? I dropped my finger and didn't bother answering the idiot back.

Then the doors in question opened and a human wearing a dark uniform and carrying a clipboard walked through them, confirming what Mr Grumpy Goat had just said. As he walked down towards the cells he slowed and peered at the mass of mythical madness in front of him. Little sucker still seemed in awe of the ugly gits, how sweet. He pulled up his clipboard before calling out "Vincent Talitine?"

I pushed myself off my seat as it was a chore and smoothly moved towards him. "Sup?"

He looked back down at his clipboard, then up at me, then back down. "Huh. I didn't know you even got Male Sirens. You learn something new every day."

I frowned and said, "I'm sorry. I didn't catch what you said. Could you come closer?" I felt my gills ripple as I got the shivers. The human looked up and nodded, a big smile on his face as he stepped closer towards the cell.

They never learn.

[WP] In the far distant future, science has advanced markedly and explored our entire universe and found the edge of reality. Now, you and one other scientist are about to venture out into Beyond.

Aurora glanced over with a nervous smile at her partner Kelvin. He stared wide eyed out the window as two mechanical arms of their space station extended thousands of miles into space and began the process of peeling open the edge of their universe. It would be something like if you ripped a hole in a bed sheet using only your hands. Kelvin averted his gaze from the window and noticed a tremble in Aurora's lip

This is going to work he said with a re assuring smile. Aurora took a deep breath and nodded in agreement.

I know, I'm just nervous about what comes after that...

Kelvin didn't have an answer for that, he couldn't do anything but look away and reanalyze the launching sequence for the satellite, his way of pretending like he wasn't just as nervous as his partner.

Sagan will do it's job the best that it can, it's a damn strong little satellite and based on our predictions about the multiverse I'd bet good money it works perfectly. he finally said with almost no emotion behind his words, he wasn't good at faking confidence but Aurora aprreciated his efforts. The truth was that netiher of them had any idea of what to expect when the giant mechanical arms of space station Bagger288 finally tore open the universe, they knew that they would have enough time to launch their satellite into the unknown before the hole in the universe sealed itself up. They knew that they could receive communications from the satellite in the form of Kaku waves, a very strong type of radio signal that could travel through the multiverse. That was all they had though, they had no idea if the satellite could even survive in the unkown conditions of the multiverse and more than that, they still weren't sure if there was even anything to observe outside their universe besides Kaku waves themselves. The next 10 minutes would show humanity just how far they had come, and just how far they had to go. Kelvin inputted the launch command for the Sagan and the countdown appeared on the window backlit by the intense burst of light created by the space station's arms burning as they worked to open the door to the unkown. They would be viewing the event using cameras mounted along the edges of the Bagger288's arms. A few minutes of silence passed and the two friends stared nervously at the numbers ticking down.

I thought, we'd have something more profound to say Aurora joked as she tried to ease the tension

We should have brought a poet Kelvin responded with a smile

I think we'll let nature be our poet for this journey Aurora responded

How profound. Kelvin quipped with a smirk.

The two shared another laugh followed by another few minutes of tense silence. Sagan's launch sequence dropped to its final 10 seconds and as it launched the two scientists watched it literally blaze a trail through space to the edge of the only reality humanity had ever known. The Bagger288 finally tore open the universe and revealed a kaleidoscope tapestry of new colors and geometric patterns; it opened the universe just in time for the Sagan satellite to venture into the blinding beauty of a new frontier for mankind. Kelvin and Aurora both cried silently as they witnessed the greatest event in the history of the universe. The hole in the universe sealed itself up and the two scientists hugged each other before regaining their composure only to lose it again when they started getting a radio response from the Sagan. Tiny little morse code like beeps signaled the satellite was surviving and working.

Aurora Nye and Kelvin DeGrasse Tyson were the first humans to observe the wonders of the multiverse, their work lead to the greatest scentific advancements their universe had ever known. Although they never lived long enough to fully understand the sacred knowledge of the multiverse, it was their beautiful curiosity for the unknown that helped unite all the galaxies of an entire universe in peace. 100 years later, when the first alien universes were discovered, they were named Nye and degrasse Tyson in honor of the two great sceintists who helped open our Universe's eyes to the beauty of the multiverse.

“Cut the crap, Burton, you’re sending me out there to die.” James steepled his hands, letting them hover just under his nose. They were covered in thick calluses, aged from years of masonry work. He had been out of a cockpit, out of the politics of Leviathan for so long, a small part of him was surprised when Burton showed up on his door. Then again, a small part wasn’t.

Burton continued, “You were a hero once James, the champion of the 3 star systems. Every boy grew up wanting to be you, every girl-- you get the picture. Don’t you want that again?”

It was ludicrous to James, sending a man in his 40’s out on an exploration mission. Sending anyone out into that void seemed like a special kind of madness, and the thought of perpetual dark sent a spark down his spine. “It’s bullshit is what it is. Just because I’m out of the Forum doesn’t mean I don’t know what those cyber-brained “immortals” are up to. They’re afraid of my reports after the war. They’re afraid of people coming to talk with me to confirm what I wrote all those years ago. So they’re sending me to hell. Alone.”

Burton was visibly red, but sadly it wasn’t from the heat. It was always toasty along the equator, but today was unique. Some cruel gate had burst open and Burton crawled out of it to give James the news. “You’re family will be compensated of course. And you won’t be alone, James, the ship will have several drones and a Folder. You always got along with them-- they’re not hard on the eyes either.”

James’ steeple gave way to fists, “You can’t ‘get along’ with them, they don’t talk back. We made them to get us past light-speed, and the only thing we taught them was pain. I don’t even think the things know we talk to them. Everything is inputs, commands, squiggly mathematical factors and sums to them. I won’t do it.”

“James, as your friend, please make this easier on yourself.” Burton reached a gloved hand toward James’ shoulder. It was slapped away, the echo of which James could still hear as the drones woke him at the outer rim of the last galaxy.

“Drink ‘em if you got ‘em, ‘cause we won’t be getting any more.” The drone returned a buzzing noise, meant to simulate a cat’s purr or some such nonsense. Mechanical pantomimes where the last thing James needed, but it looked like that’s all there would be now. The navigational display showed a discomforting red-dash where everything came to an end, conveniently marketed as “Beyond” by the Forum. There was nothing beyond about it. The edge of everything humanity knew about the universe. Everything past that was an all-consuming darkness.

He swiveled in his chair and broke off the edge of a ration. The rest of the bar he waved in front of the tank suspended above him. “Want some?” He knew the Folders were suspended in a nutrient bath, that she probably didn’t even know he was there, but it felt necessary. Stretching back, he stared for a while, tracing out the contours of scales grafted over almost translucent skin. Each Folder was given raven-black hair, and this one had enough to cover most of the fin-like protrusions on the sides of her head. She looked delicate, almost refined, like a mineral cut into the shape of some ancient sea-nymph.

A buzzer sounded and James realized he had fallen asleep. The line came and went, the readout marking “border crossed, maintaining course” to celebrate the end of his world. Stars were a thing of the past, and along with them the ease of traveling faster than light. Conventional speeds would have to suffice now. “Well, I can’t complain about the view.” He settled back into the chair and returned to dreams of home.

Turbulence rocked James from his seat, spilling him out over the cold, steel floor. “The hell was that!” Standing, he looked out the view-port at the inky darkness. A flat emptiness spread out forever. He punched up the readout from the Folder, and a series of notations scrolled past. Something had grazed the starboard paneling, but it wasn’t enough to damage the hull. “There shouldn’t be anything out here. And there definitely shouldn’t be something moving as fast as us.” He brought up the speed controls, nothing had changed.

A second shudder rumbled through the ship, and James stared at the display in disbelief. Large, cold letters scrolled across the screen. “Afraid.” Language was never programmed into Folders, but there it was. Fear, from one of them out here in the vast nothing of the void. He turned his head up, his gaze returned by solid black eyes. He could tell she was shivering in the tube, that whatever sensory input was coming from outside of the ship was worth that reaction. He snapped his head back down, glaring out the view-port. There was a dim glow far in the distance, bobbing back and forth. Lines poured across the panel, waves of the same word crashing from top to bottom. The light drew closer, growing into an small sun. Yet the glow seemed cold, and James’ hair bristled until he broke his gaze.

“What is it! Tell me something I can understand. It’s what you were brought with to do, you worthless fish-wife.” He drove his knuckles against the display, leaving behind a rivulet of blood. “At least change course. As it is, we’ll hit the damn thing!” The light dominated the view-port, but the navigational computer simply kept repeating itself. James screamed for what he thought was the last few moments of his life, but the light vanished as abruptly as it appeared. Darkness once again loomed in front of him. Displays bled out complex algorithms, the Folder’s eyes were once again shut, and James was left alone to question his sanity.

“What is out here with me?"
